chapters.title: Chapter 1: Fundamentals of Generative Modeling
chapters.description: Introduces core concepts and families of generative models used in modern machine learning, providing the high-level background necessary to understand why diffusion models are used for image synthesis.
subtopics: Definition of generative modeling and objective types (likelihood-based, implicit)
Overview of major families: VAEs, GANs, autoregressive models, energy-based models
Basic training objectives: maximum likelihood, adversarial loss, reconstruction loss
Qualitative trade-offs: fidelity vs diversity, mode collapse, likelihood vs perceptual quality
Evaluation basics: sample quality, diversity, and evaluation pitfalls

chapters.title: Chapter 2: Diffusion and Score-Based Generative Models
chapters.description: Detailed coverage of diffusion processes and score-based modeling: forward noising, reverse denoising, training objectives, and practical sampling algorithms used in modern image diffusion models.
subtopics: Forward noising (diffusion) process and marginal statistics
Reverse denoising process and connection to score matching
DDPM (Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models) and derivation of training loss
Score-based generative modeling and stochastic differential equations (SDEs)
Sampling strategies: ancestral sampling, deterministic samplers (DDIM), and classifier-free guidance
Latent diffusion vs pixel-space diffusion (motivation and differences)

chapters.title: Chapter 3: Text-to-Image Pipelines and Multimodal Representations
chapters.description: Covers the components and data flows in text-conditioned image generation systems: text encoders, image latents, cross-attention mechanisms, and exemplar models like Stable Diffusion and DALL·E variants.
subtopics: Text encoders and multimodal embeddings (e.g., CLIP encoder basics)
Conditioning mechanisms in diffusion models: concatenation, cross-attention, classifier guidance
Latent autoencoders (VAE, VQ-GAN) and their role in latent diffusion pipelines
Typical UNet or encoder-decoder denoiser architectures used in diffusion models
High-level pipelines of systems like Stable Diffusion, Imagen, and DALL·E2
Runtime considerations and inference pipeline for text-conditioned sampling

chapters.title: Chapter 4: Linear Algebra for Neural Networks and Geometric Views
chapters.description: Presents linear-algebraic and geometric notions applied to neural network weights and activations, including vector norms, inner products, normalization, and the notion of neuron directionality.
subtopics: Vectors, norms (L2), inner products and cosine similarity
Interpreting neurons/filters as weight vectors in R^d
Normalization of weights and activations; effects of unit-norm constraints
Angles between vectors and geometric interpretation of similarity
Consequences of scaling vs direction change on linear transforms

chapters.title: Chapter 5: Angular Representations and Hyperspherical Geometry
chapters.description: Introduces hyperspherical representations and the role of angular measures in representation learning, including the definition and implications of hyperspherical energy.
subtopics: Unit hypersphere and normalization of feature/weight vectors
Cosine similarity and angular metrics as semantic measures
SphereNet and angular softmax ideas (using directions for classification)
Definition of hyperspherical energy and intuition (pairwise angular relations)
Implications of hyperspherical energy: neuron uniformity, redundancy, and representation structure

chapters.title: Chapter 6: Orthogonal Matrices and the Orthogonal Group
chapters.description: Covers algebraic and geometric properties of orthogonal transformations (rotations/reflections), their effect on inner products and angles, and relevant group-theoretic terminology.
subtopics: Definition and properties of orthogonal matrices: R^T R = I
Preservation of inner products, norms, and angles under orthogonal transforms
Determinant ±1 distinction: rotations (SO(n)) vs reflections
Orthogonal group O(n) and special orthogonal group SO(n)
Composition and inverse properties of orthogonal matrices

chapters.title: Chapter 7: Orthogonal Parameterizations and the Cayley Transform
chapters.description: Presents practical parameterizations of orthogonal matrices for learning, with emphasis on the Cayley transform, skew-symmetric matrices, block-diagonal constructions, and their computational properties.
subtopics: Skew-symmetric matrices and their relationship to orthogonal matrices
Cayley parameterization: R = (I + Q)(I - Q)^{-1} with Q = -Q^T
Limitations of Cayley: inability to represent reflections (determinant -1) and numerical considerations
Neumann series approximation for matrix inverse and small-Q expansion
Block-diagonal and block-sharing parameterizations to reduce parameter count
Practical considerations: initialization to identity, numerical stability

chapters.title: Chapter 8: Optimization on Manifolds and Orthogonality Constraints
chapters.description: Describes optimization methods suitable for constrained matrix variables (orthogonality), including projected gradient methods, retractions, and other manifold-aware techniques.
subtopics: Constrained optimization vs unconstrained optimization
Optimization on Stiefel and orthogonal manifolds: retractions and geodesics
Projected gradient descent for orthogonality constraints
Differentiable orthogonalization methods (e.g., Gram–Schmidt, QR, Cayley-based updates)
Trade-offs: computational cost vs strict orthogonality enforcement

chapters.title: Chapter 9: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning Techniques
chapters.description: Surveys methods for adapting large pretrained models efficiently: additive adapters, low-rank updates, LoRA-style reparameterizations, and other adapter-style approaches relevant to finetuning diffusion models.
subtopics: Motivation for parameter-efficient finetuning (compute, storage, overfitting)
Adapter modules, prefix tuning, and prompt tuning
LoRA: low-rank additive updates and parameterization details
Pivotal Tuning and DreamBooth-style adaptation for image models
Comparison of multiplicative vs additive weight updates and their effects

chapters.title: Chapter 10: Convolutional and Transformer Layers: Weight Structure and Finetuning Targets
chapters.description: Examines structural details of convolutional and Transformer layers (attention, MLPs) and explains common choices for which weights to adapt during finetuning.
subtopics: Standard convolutional layer weights and interpretation as channel-wise neuron vectors
Depthwise and pointwise convolutions and channel-wise parameterization
Transformer attention: query/key/value/projection matrices and where to apply adapters
Fully connected (MLP) layers and per-neuron parameterization
Practical considerations: memory, compute, and where low-rank or orthogonal transforms can be applied

chapters.title: Chapter 11: Signal Processing Intuition: Fourier Transform, Phase, and Magnitude
chapters.description: Explains 2D Fourier decomposition of images and the semantic role of phase versus magnitude, providing intuition for why angular information may preserve semantic content.
subtopics: 2D discrete Fourier transform (DFT) and frequency domain representation
Magnitude spectrum vs phase spectrum and visual reconstruction experiments
Role of phase in preserving structure and semantics of images
Analogies between phase information and angular/neuron-direction information
Limitations of the analogy and when it does and does not apply

chapters.title: Chapter 12: Matrix Calculus and Differentiation through Matrix Functions
chapters.description: Presents matrix derivatives and backpropagation through matrix inverses and other matrix-valued functions relevant for implementing differentiable orthogonal parameterizations.
subtopics: Basic matrix derivatives and useful identities (d(Ax), d(AT), product rules)
Derivative of matrix inverse and stability considerations
Backpropagation through parameterizations that require matrix inverse (Cayley)
Efficient automatic differentiation strategies for matrix operations
Gradient clipping and numerical conditioning for matrix-valued parameters

chapters.title: Chapter 13: Regularization, Stability, and Convergence in Finetuning
chapters.description: Discusses techniques and principles to maintain pretrained model abilities during finetuning, avoid collapse, and ensure stable and efficient convergence.
subtopics: Overfitting risks in few-shot finetuning and remedies (weight decay, data augmentation)
Small learning-rate regimes and implicit constraints on parameter drift
Explicit constraints and regularizers (distance to pretrained weights, parameter norms)
Stability issues in generative model finetuning and collapse modes
Measuring convergence speed and robustness across seeds

chapters.title: Chapter 14: Evaluation Metrics for Generative Image Quality and Control
chapters.description: Covers standard quantitative metrics and practical protocols for assessing image generation quality, subject fidelity, prompt fidelity, and control consistency in conditional generation tasks.
subtopics: Perceptual and distributional metrics: FID, IS (overview and caveats)
Representation-based similarity metrics: CLIP score for text-image alignment
Feature-matching metrics: DINO, LPIPS for diversity and perceptual distance
Task-specific control metrics: IoU, F1 for structure consistency, landmark L2 for pose control
Human evaluation protocols, seed averaging, and statistical significance in generative evaluations

chapters.title: Chapter 15: Experimental Methodology and Reproducibility for Generative Model Research
chapters.description: Guidance on designing experiments, choosing baselines, conducting ablation studies, and reporting results reproducibly for finetuning large generative models.
subtopics: Selecting baselines and ensuring fair comparisons (matching parameter budgets/targets)
Dataset splits, few-shot protocols, and data-efficiency experiments
Ablation studies: hyperparameters, parameter counts, and block/ rank choices
Reporting standard deviations, multiple seeds, and failure cases
Computational considerations and reproducible code/seed reporting
